analysis:
The PR changes only docs/developer/test.md (head lines 141-153). It rewrites the CI build-cache description: PRs now restore the base branch's cache and save nothing, and only pushes to dev or master save one. It also adds a paragraph saying the MiMo audio gate (testNativeAudioRelease) runs in the last provider shard only when its inputs change (MIMO_AUDIO in scripts/ci-component-paths.py) and on every master push.

This is documentation only. It adds no runtime code, provider keys, coordinator wire behavior, attestation, authorization, cache-storage or fan-helper change. I found no regression against T-041 (prefix cache/SSD tier), TB-011, TB-012 or the other trust boundaries. The retained guidance still says to keep tests isolated, never use production cache roots or keys, and not to run against a live provider. The doc does not claim qualification for production.

The documented CI change (PRs no longer save caches, which narrows cache poisoning from PR builds) is a security-neutral-to-positive hardening. Whether it is actually implemented in the workflows and scripts (build.md#ci-caching, scripts/ci-component-paths.py, the workflow files) is outside the supplied evidence. If those files differ from this description, the doc would be inaccurate, but that is not a security finding.

No threat-model update is needed. The remainder of the file (lines 1-141 and 154-927) is unchanged context. I did not review it for new behavior and found no new security assertions there.
